comment:
* A proxy over read-only device state that allows things like system properties, elapsed
     * realtime clock to be faked for tests.

methods.name: int getNitzUpdateSpacingMillis()
methods.comment:
* If the elapsed realtime between two NITZ signals is greater than this value then the
         * second signal cannot be ignored.

methods.name: int getNitzUpdateDiffMillis()
methods.comment:
* If Unix epoch time between two NITZ signals is greater than this value then the second
         * signal cannot be ignored.

methods.name: int getNitzNetworkDisconnectRetentionMillis()
methods.comment:
* If the device connects to a telephony network and was disconnected from a telephony * network for less than this time, a previously received NITZ signal can be restored. * *

The restored NITZ may not be from the same network as the current network. It is * intended to be a relatively small value to allow for brief disconnections. Larger values * increase the likelihood that the device has moved to a different network and/or time * zone.

methods.name: boolean getIgnoreNitz()
methods.comment: * Returns true if the {@code gsm.ignore-nitz} system property is set to "yes".

methods.name: long elapsedRealtimeMillis()
methods.comment: * Returns the same value as {@link SystemClock#elapsedRealtime()}.

methods.name: long currentTimeMillis()
methods.comment: * Returns the same value as {@link System#currentTimeMillis()}.
